avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone secretion, decreasing potassium excretion and increasing serum levels; potassium supplements amplify hyperkalemia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid potassium supplements unless specifically prescribed by clinician; monitor serum potassium regularly

avoid_supplements.name: NSAIDs (including ibuprofen, naproxen)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal blood flow and increase potassium retention; combined use increases hyperkalemia risk and reduces antihypertensive efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid NSAIDs; use acetaminophen or topical NSAIDs as alternatives; if NSAIDs necessary, use lowest dose for shortest duration with increased monitoring

avoid_supplements.name: ACE inhibitor herbal supplements (licorice, yohimbe)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Licorice causes sodium retention and potassium loss with compensatory hyperkalemia risk; yohimbe increases blood pressure opposing lisinopril's effect
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue licorice and yohimbe; choose alternative supplements with clinician approval

caution_supplements.name: Garlic supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate hypotensive effects through vasodilation; additive blood pressure lowering possible
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure; adjust lisinopril dose if significant hypotension develops

caution_supplements.name: CoQ10
caution_supplements.mechanism: May cause modest additional blood pressure reduction; theoretical synergistic effect
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure regularly; inform clinician of concurrent use

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May enhance vasodilation and potentiate hypotensive effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure; coordinate supplementation with clinician

avoid_foods.name: High-potassium foods (excessive intake)
avoid_foods.mechanism: ACE inhibitors impair potassium excretion; excessive dietary potassium increases hyperkalemia risk, particularly in renal impairment
avoid_foods.action: Limit potassium-rich foods (bananas, oranges, spinach, potatoes, tomatoes) to normal dietary amounts; avoid potassium salt substitutes

caution_foods.name: Moderate potassium-containing foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Normal intake generally safe but contributes to overall potassium load; risk increases with renal dysfunction or concurrent medications
caution_foods.action: Monitor serum potassium at baseline and periodically; adjust intake based on lab results and renal function

caution_foods.name: Licorice-containing foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Licorice causes sodium retention opposing lisinopril's antihypertensive effect
caution_foods.action: Minimize licorice candy and licorice root-containing products

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum potassium, creatinine, and blood pressure at baseline and regularly during therapy, especially in patients with renal impairment, diabetes, or concurrent use of other renin-angiotensin system inhibitors. Counsel patients on signs of hyperkalemia (weakness, palpitations, shortness of breath) and angioedema (facial swelling, difficulty breathing).
